Eczema.name: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
Eczema.description: A chronic inflammatory skin condition characterized by dry, pruritic (itchy), and erythematous patches, often occurring in flexural areas (inner elbows, behind knees).
common_symptoms: Intense pruritus (itching), particularly at night
Erythematous, dry, cracked, or scaly patches
Excoriations from scratching, leading to lichenification
Occasional clear oozing or crusting during acute flares
risk_factors: Personal or family history of atopy (asthma, allergic rhinitis)
Skin barrier dysfunction (filaggrin gene mutations)
Environmental triggers: soaps, detergents, low humidity, stress
management_tips: Frequent application of thick emollients (ointments or heavy creams)
Short lukewarm baths with soap-free cleansers
Short-term topical corticosteroids or calcineurin inhibitors for flares
Avoid known allergens, wool fabrics, and harsh detergents
red_flags: Signs of secondary bacterial infection (honey-colored crusting, pustules, spreading redness)

Psoriasis.name: Psoriasis (Plaque Psoriasis)
Psoriasis.description: An immune-mediated chronic inflammatory skin disease causing hyperproliferation of keratinocytes, presenting as sharply demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery-white scales.
common_symptoms: Well-demarcated raised plaques with thick, micaceous (silvery) scales
Auspitz sign (pinpoint bleeding when scales are removed)
Common on extensor surfaces (knees, elbows), scalp, and lumbosacral region
Nail pitting, onycholysis, or subungual hyperkeratosis
risk_factors: Genetic predisposition (HLA-Cw6 association)
Triggers: physical trauma (Koebner phenomenon), streptococcal infection, stress
Smoking, obesity, and certain medications (beta-blockers, lithium)
management_tips: Topical therapies: high-potency corticosteroids combined with vitamin D analogues (calcipotriol)
Topical retinoids and keratolytic agents (salicylic acid)
Phototherapy (narrowband UVB) for moderate-to-severe disease
Systemic agents or biologics (anti-TNF, anti-IL-17, anti-IL-23) for refractory cases
red_flags: Psoriatic arthritis symptoms (joint stiffness, swelling, dactylitis)
Erythrodermic psoriasis (>90% body surface area involvement with fever)
Generalized pustular psoriasis requiring urgent emergency care

Melanoma.name: Melanoma (Malignant Melanoma)
Melanoma.urgency_badge: 🔴 High Urgency / Immediate Biopsy & Oncology Referral
Melanoma.description: A high-grade malignant cutaneous neoplasm arising from melanocytes. It is the deadliest form of skin cancer, characterized by rapid growth, asymmetry, irregular borders, and variable pigmentation.
common_symptoms: Asymmetry: one half does not match the other
Border irregularity: notched, scalloped, or poorly defined edges
Color variation: multiple shades of brown, black, blue, red, or white
Diameter: usually >6 mm, though can be smaller in early stages
Evolving: lesion changing in size, shape, color, or developing bleeding/elevation
risk_factors: Excessive cumulative or intermittent UV exposure and history of sunburns
Fitzpatrick skin phototypes I and II (fair skin, freckling, light eyes)
High total nevus count (>50 moles) or presence of atypical/dysplastic nevi
Personal or family history of melanoma (CDKN2A mutations)
management_tips: Immediate urgent surgical excisional biopsy with appropriate clinical margins
Histopathologic staging (Breslow thickness, ulceration status, mitotic rate)
Sentinel lymph node biopsy for intermediate/thick lesions
Systemic targeted therapy (BRAF/MEK inhibitors) or immunotherapy (PD-1/CTLA-4 blockers)
red_flags: Rapid growth, ulceration, spontaneous bleeding, or new satellite pigmentation
Any 'ugly duckling' mole that looks markedly distinct from other lesions

Basal Cell Carcinoma.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC)
Basal Cell Carcinoma.description: The most common cutaneous malignancy arising from the basal layer of the epidermis. Rarely metastasizes but can cause significant local tissue destruction if left untreated.
common_symptoms: Pearly, translucent nodule with rolled or beaded borders
Prominent arborizing telangiectasias (spider veins) on the lesion surface
Central ulceration ('rodent ulcer') with easy bleeding upon minor trauma
Non-healing sore that crusts, bleeds, and recurs in sun-exposed areas
risk_factors: Chronic, long-term ultraviolet radiation exposure
Light skin complexion (Fitzpatrick I-III)
Advanced age, immunosuppression, or history of radiation therapy
management_tips: Standard surgical excision with margin verification
Mohs micrographic surgery for cosmetically sensitive areas (face, nose, eyelids)
Topical imiquimod, 5-fluorouracil, or cryotherapy for superficial variants
Hedgehog pathway inhibitors (vismodegib) for locally advanced cases
red_flags: Rapid enlargement near vital anatomical structures (periorbital, perinasal)
Recurrent bleeding and perineural invasion symptoms (pain, numbness)

Seborrheic Keratosis.name: Seborrheic Keratosis
Seborrheic Keratosis.description: A very common, harmless benign epithelial tumor of the skin, frequently presenting as a 'stuck-on', warty or greasy plaque in older adults.
common_symptoms: Well-circumscribed, 'stuck-on' appearance as if pressed onto the skin
Verrucous (warty), granular, or greasy surface texture
Color ranges from tan, flesh-colored, yellowish to dark brown or black
Horn pseudocysts visible on dermoscopy
risk_factors: Aging (common over 50 years)
Genetic predisposition
Cumulative sun exposure
management_tips: Reassurance of benign nature; no mandatory medical treatment required
Cryosurgery (liquid nitrogen) or curettage if irritated by clothing or for cosmetic reasons
Histopathologic confirmation if lesion is highly pigmented and difficult to distinguish from melanoma
red_flags: Sudden explosive eruption of hundreds of pruritic SK lesions (Sign of Leser-Trélat, potential paraneoplastic marker)
Atypical color variegation, asymmetry, or spontaneous ulceration

Acne Vulgaris.name: Acne Vulgaris
Acne Vulgaris.urgency_badge: 🟢 Low Urgency / Primary or Derm Care
Acne Vulgaris.description: A disorder of the pilosebaceous unit characterized by microcomedones, open/closed comedones (blackheads/whiteheads), inflammatory papules, pustules, and nodulocystic lesions.
common_symptoms: Comedones (open blackheads and closed whiteheads)
Inflammatory erythematous papules and pustules
Deep painful cysts and nodules in severe forms
Common distribution on face, chest, upper back, and shoulders
risk_factors: Androgen excess or hormonal fluctuations (puberty, menstrual cycle)
Excess sebum production and follicular hyperkeratinization
Cutibacterium acnes colonization and cutaneous inflammation
Comedogenic cosmetic products
management_tips: Topical retinoids (adapalene, tretinoin) combined with benzoyl peroxide
Topical or oral antibiotics (doxycycline) for inflammatory lesions
Hormonal therapy (combined oral contraceptives, spironolactone) for females
Oral isotretinoin for severe, recalcitrant, or scarring nodular acne
red_flags: Severe cystic scarring leading to psychological distress
Sudden acute fever with severe ulcerating acne (Acne Fulminans)

Fungal Infection.name: Fungal Infection (Tinea / Dermatophytosis)
Fungal Infection.description: A superficial fungal infection of keratinized tissue (stratum corneum) caused by dermatophytes (Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton), presenting as annular scaling plaques.
common_symptoms: Annular ('ringworm') erythematous lesion with active scaly advancing border
Central clearing giving a ring-like appearance
Mild to moderate pruritus (itching)
Occasional satellite lesions or peripheral scaling
risk_factors: Warm, humid climates and occlusive clothing
Contact sports (wrestling), sharing towels, or contact with infected pets
Compromised immunity or diabetes mellitus
management_tips: Topical antifungals (terbinafine, clotrimazole, ketoconazole) applied 1-2 cm beyond the border for 2-4 weeks
Keep affected skin clean, dry, and well-ventilated
Oral antifungals (terbinafine, itraconazole) for extensive, scalp (tinea capitis), or nail involvement (onychomycosis)
Avoid topical steroids alone, which can cause 'tinea incognito'
red_flags: Secondary bacterial cellulitis or extensive uncontained spread
Persistent non-response after 4 weeks of standard antifungal therapy

Healthy Skin.name: Healthy / Benign Nevus (Normal Skin)
Healthy Skin.description: Normal cutaneous tissue or common acquired melanocytic nevus exhibiting symmetric architecture, uniform coloration, sharp regular borders, and stable dimensions.
common_symptoms: Symmetric round or oval shape
Evenly distributed light to dark brown pigmentation
Smooth, distinct borders with normal adjacent skin architecture
Asymptomatic (no pain, bleeding, persistent itching, or active ulceration)
risk_factors: Standard genetic background and baseline sun exposure
management_tips: Perform monthly head-to-toe skin self-examinations
Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30+) application
Wear UV-protective clothing and sunglasses during peak sunlight hours
Annual routine total-body skin check with a healthcare provider
red_flags: Any noticeable evolution in size, border symmetry, color variegation, or new symptoms
